title: Studio: a Chinese display name derives no identifier — New Package leaves Package ID and namespace empty, New Object leaves 标识 empty, and Add Field names the field field_10
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"marchtian"} -->
_Requested by **田騏** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi?thread=cmsg_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi7SkqaNxU2Ef8P2DMmp2hPJ)_

Found while building a small app end to end in Studio (zh-CN UI), on objectui `main` @ `6fb31dc` against objectstack `main` @ `b9c7a8f`.

## Steps and observations

1. Studio → **新建软件包(可写基座)**. Type `体验评审` as 显示名称. **软件包 ID** and **对象命名空间** stay empty (their help text says they are filled from the display name until edited). Typing `Review Lab` instead fills `com.default.review-lab` / `review_lab` at once.
2. In the new package → **新建对象**. Type `反馈` as 对象名称: **标识** stays empty. `Feedback` fills `feedback`.
3. On the object → **添加字段**, display name `满意度`, type 评分 → 创建. The field is created with API name **`field_10`**, visible in the field inspector and later in the publish diff (`+ 满意度 field_10`) and in the list view column picker.

## Why it matters

The console is localized for zh-CN, so a Chinese author naturally types Chinese labels. Today that author gets either a blank required identifier with no hint about why it did not fill in, or an identifier like `field_10` that is permanent once published (it becomes the column name and the API field everyone integrates against).

## Suggested direction

Any of these would fix the experience; they are not exclusive:

- derive a slug from a transliteration when the label has no ASCII letters (the platform already ships pinyin support for search, `PinyinSearchPlugin` on the server);
- when no slug can be derived, say so next to the identifier field ("请填写英文标识" style) instead of leaving it silently blank;
- never mint a positional name like `field_N` without showing the author that it happened and inviting a rename before the first publish.

Also seen on the same dialog: the default package id prefix is `com.default.`, which is unlikely to be what anyone wants to ship; a prompt for the org's reverse-domain prefix would avoid it.
